activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet them. This   
      continues all the way around the circle.
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. Put the   
 items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two pictures on the board   
      instead.
• Say: Di Funoomaf ufe, múmikaam moololaal moo emmi mati '' Sínukuruŋas '' . Wahaw   
  wammi di titoorey yati fúliibaf ubabaj fúkaw bee di múmikaam moololaal.  
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Ure waawu?       
• Call on a pupil at rando to answer.
• Say:  Waawu pan uŋoolen uregom mati ure?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: Ure waawu ufelolaal?
• Give pupils one minute to think. You may suggest they close their eyes to picture their   
 response. Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on 3 pupils at random,  
 Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and allow every  
 pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the week.

Activity
• Play: SONG OR GAME RELATING TO THE THEME

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Alphabet I-Spy
• Gather all of the letter cards of the letters that have been learned. Place the letter cards in 
different places around the room where the pupils can see the pictures.
• Give pupils a minute to look around to see where the picture cards have been placed.
• Say: Pan jikaanaal fáreed fan koone  ''kálulen '' Pan  iwonk eciika nampi jijukumi 
búwuloorumab booliyo, jipop man jiñuur buwuloorumab dimoro. Jiliikaal mo. Nijujuk fúrim 
fabaje kayelak/ a /. 
• Give pupils a chance to find the picture.
• Say: Eciikaay ''a'' etooŋumi fúrimaf ''atampa ''. Jiregaal siñakon '' a '',  ''atampa ''
• Repeat two times slowly while pointing to the key word.
• Continue with a few keywords. Be sure to go over letters that have been learned thus far.

activities.title: Letter of the Week
activities.content:
Learning Letter: "a" "A"
• Write the small letter "a" very big on the board. Point to the letter.
• Say: Eciikaay uye nootaale ekaan di fúnoomaf ufe. Kayelak kooliyo / a /. Jiregaal  siñakon /a/.
• Point to the letter on the board or letter card, say the sound, have pupils repeat 3 times 
slowly.
• Write the capital letter "A" very big on the board. Point to the capital letter.
• Say: Eciikaay yákoney yooye. Yoo poop yommi /a / .Pan jijukaal  yo di fúcitumaf fati  
kasankenak, kareesak kati anaw mba kareesak kati banab.
• Point to the letter on the board or letter card, say the sound, have pupils repeat 3 times 
slowly.
• Point to the small letter "a" on the board or letter card again.
• Say: Ñajuupoe, moo njijukaalemi eeno di kurimak.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: Wulaal bee ebill kaliitikenak kati eciikey ureesaw woololaal. Ootaajaat etooŋey pan 
úlantwulaal uñenaw woololaal
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 10 seconds. 
Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground. 
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters correctly. Provide 
guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for the pupil to trace.

lessons.homework: Ask learners to teach their family members the letter name and sound they learnt today.

activities.title: Vocabulary
activities.content:
Teach and Discuss New Words
• Words: 
Kásiyak   Mumelam   
• Say: Nuliitikenaaleliikiten kúrim kúnkul man kurambenolaal  úlawlaal uregaw jak. 
      Babaj kúrim kupinaay  kabaje fúkaw di karegak kaceeŋumi man uliitikenaal.
• Say the first vocabulary word, but do NOT write it on the board. Then have pupils say the word 
aloud. Repeat two more times.
• Ask pupils what they know about the word. Share the meaning of the word, using gestures or 
illustrations to support understanding. 
• If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language.
• Repeat all steps with remaining word.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Noolenaal man karegak kootum kaanoak.
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say: Di búyejeti,joonen buwuloorumab banokoorum nan man uwoonoorumi man karegak  
kootum kaanoak. Waawu nujukumi?
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind. 
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they are 

visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. Choose a good 
example you heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.
• Say: Ñaa  unaamenaal uwuloorumaw wati di karegak  buu wunokoorumi eeno.
• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: Waawu nujukumi di buwuloorumab wanokoorumi nan man jijukumi di úyejetuul . 
• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at random 
asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the picture and the 
story.
• Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Nan uliikaalemi, nuliikaaleliik furim fákon fákon. Karegak kubabaj kurim kajuupoe 
kaliikeyimi fákon fákon di katoj kanoosani.
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud  
• Say: Liik tebo 
      [ Karegak kati ejoosooray di kásiyak kati mumelam ]
• Read aloud the story.
 
Ejeesooraay di Kásiyak kati mumelam
Lakomi lakomi di lakomi tokos!
Babaj jijoosoora jalinloe koonejo Linlo. Funak fákon fáboliye wút, Linlo baraanab di busofool 
máamak.  Butumab di kumerak di kusay rat, tan malegenam mommi namammaŋ baraan. Linlo 
nammi,'pan ikob kalubak. Bare kunak kajuupoe di kuwuuj, mumel mulet.  Balaab di bufaŋumi 
man búboliye, érusey di enag dimoro, moomanoosani doodu man saye.
Linlo najawumi eñesey mumelam.Najaw awuuj urambaaw, naremboor kukoobaak. Nafús 
fáteemenaaf fati utojaw di eñesey yati mumelam, bare ayetut ajuk mumel.
Ñaa, Linlo najukumi waaf di fátaamenaaf fati búbaaraab wasayoo. Di kammi kama kásiyak kati 
mumel kájupi di fúrul fafanlene.
Natey bee too man aan, "Buu pan iŋoolen iraan di kásiyak uke?"
Linlo naraagal ecuutey yati mumelam ñetum di fúrontoon, bare butumab boola butiititiiti 
máamak. Ayetut abaj hani mumel. ñaa nañesumi ekoobaay man araagal aleeb di fúrulaf man mbi 
fukonten yo étaas, bare uñenaw woola ulabolabo máamak. Bee iñee mumel mulet.
Linlo alaañut bálamuk, Nalaañ ajegoor najuk mukoobaam. Nabaj siwoonoor. Nakatenumi 
mukoobaam di kásiyak ñákon ñákon. Piyout,Mumelam di mutooŋ kayito fatiya.
Di múlamukaam, mumelam di múyuwowulomi di kásiyak. Linlo nanajo akot kásiyak man araan 
araan biyok gáamulool. Namaayoor man akammi man aŋoolen araan.
Ñaa Linlo najaw amaal, di kasuumak di fupooñ, bee di kajonjoor mati mukeen.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Factual Question: Review All 
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the following factual 
questions:
• Question 1: Linlo waawu nalakoe eñes? [ Mumelam ]  
• Question 2: Linlo béy najukey mumelam? (di kásiyak.)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help pupils find the part of the 
story that contains the answer.
• Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: Kareg kanookani kubabaj múmikaam man kuyisene. Fujuumaf foo emmi buu karegak 
koonomi? Karegak kuyisenyisen man ejoosooraay añesumi mumelam eeno.Moo kaanankaan 
kawoonoor mati ureg wajuupoe uyisenyisen buu ejoosooraay abajumi mumelam.
• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say: Fúkaaf fati karegak kati ejoosooraay di kásiyak foo emmi buu ejoosooraay ebajumi 
mumelam eeno,mati wajuupoe di karegak woo eenomi man añesumi mumelam eeno. 
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the story is 
mostly about.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board.  
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out 
in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Ecikaay uye yéy? Kayel kéy ebaje?  
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let them know if it 
is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that have been 
learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Iwonkujaat kayelak di kaan kunanaam di eciikaay yammi di bútiŋumab bati kayitak, Aw di 
apaali di jíjeetumul  kayitak di bulaakubootey  man jinaamenoor. 
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are having 
difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

Name Card #1
• Gather all the pupil name cards. 
• Say: Wulaal bee bil fáreed, Pan íyisuul karees kákon kaan jaat kareesi, nubil bee fáculey man

• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For example, "[Name] 
says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

activities.title: Comprehension: After Reading
activities.content:
Inferential Question: Why?
• Show the illustration of the story.
• Say: Niceen uregaw úyiseneriit kalaañenak too. Moo jajak ! Beñee pan uñoolen úlawul ujiker 
jaat ko: 
• Wan kati karegak kukammi .
• Wan aciikaaw amaŋumi man umanjaal.
• Ñaa ujikeraal, ''Wawu ukaane man Ejoosooraay ekob kalubak?'' ( Baraan busofo yo.) 
• Call on a pupil at random to answer the question. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. 
• Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the following inferential questions:
• Question 1: Waawu kaane man súum ejoosooraay máamak? [ Ebabaj mumel eraan] 
• Question 2: Ejoosooraay buu ebajummi mumelam di kásiyak eeno? [Yoo bakatene 
mukoobaam di kásiyak.]
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help pupils find the part of the 
story that contains the answer.

pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only

activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. The letters should be large enough for 
all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. 
After writing each letter:
• Say: Eciikaay uye yéy?  Kayel kéy ebaje?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let them know if it 
is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that have been 
learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Iwonkujaat kayelak ban nooken kayitak tan eciikaay ecila yommi, aw di apaali di jibil bee  
di búlaakubootey man jíyiisen di yan sinaamumi.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are having 
difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

• Say: Pan jikaanaal fáreed.  Pan íyiisuul karees kákon kaan jaat kooli, nubil bee fáculey man 
uwonk kareesi ban nureg kalaasey man kugoroor ñagaba.
• Hold up a name card. If the pupil is unable to recognize the name, say it aloud.
• Once the child comes up front, have them give two actions for the class. For example, 
"[Name] says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: Pan uliikenaal eciikey yati ureesaw woololaal. Ootaajaat etooŋey, pan utebenaal uñenaw 
woololaal man úsupenaal wo.
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 10 seconds. 
Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground.
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters correctly. 
• Provide guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for the pupil to trace.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Learn Print Concepts
• Find a children's storybook with an author and illustrator.
• Think about how books and stories have different parts.
• Say: Nan uliikaalemi, njijukaalejuk  wajuupoe wanaamut di kareg kanoosani.  Kareg kanoosani 
kubabaj aciika.

• Point to the author's name on the storybook.
• Say: Aciikaaw oo aciikumi karegak.  Ayima emmi aciikaaw?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by repeating, "the 
author is the person who wrote the story."
• Say: Kareg kanoosani kabajumi uwuloorumaw kubabaj ajoonenaaw.
• Point to the illustrator's name on the storybook.
• Say: Ajoonenaaw oo emmi ajoonenumi uwuloorumaaw.  
• Ayima akammi aŋaraaw ati uwuloorumaw?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by repeating, "the 
illustrator is the person who drew the pictures."
• Say: Kareg kanoosani kubabaj fujuum.
• Point to the title on the storybook.
• Say: Fujuumaf fati karegak furegolaalemi mati karegak. Waawu eenomi fujuumaf fati karegak? 
• Give the pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the

different places around the room where the pupils can see the pictures.
• Give pupils a minute to look around to see where the picture cards have been placed.
• Say: Pan  jikaanaal fáreed fati "kálulen." Pan iwonk eciikaay, nampi jijukumi buwuloorumab 
baŋarumi fujuumaf fati ammi di karegak, jibaal man jiñuur buwuloorumab dimoro. Jikaanaal 
man jijukaal. Nijujuk furim fabaje kayelak /c /.
• Give pupils a chance to find the picture.
• Say: Eciikaay '' c '' yooyu di furimaf ''bacaac''. Bonket jiregaal siñakon '' c ''  ''bacaac''
• Repeat two times slowly while pointing to the keyword.
• Continue with a few keywords. Be sure to go over letters that have been learned thus far.

activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Learning Names
• Say: We are going to learn to write our names. Before we begin, we will extend our hands. 
• Warm up exercise: have pupils push their palms together as hard as they can for 10 seconds. 
Then release and shake hands for 10 seconds. Repeat two more times.
• Give each pupil their individual name card.
• Have pupils go through the following steps: 
1. Pupils trace the letters on the name card with their fingers.
2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground. 
3. Pupils write their name on paper. 
• Monitor pupils through each step to make sure they are forming the letters correctly. Provide 
guidance as needed either verbally or by writing the letter(s) for the pupil to trace.

• Give each pupil a letter card and ask them to practice saying the letter name and sound with 
their family members.

activities.content:

 kafatak  bánaanaay
• Say: Di funoomaf ufe, múmikaam moololaal moo emmi "Kafatak." Pan uliitikenaal kúrim

kan ootaale kaliitiken di karegak.
• Say the first vocabulary word, but do NOT write it on the board. Then have pupils say the

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say: Momanosani nuliikeenaliik karegak uke, ñaa utiimalenaal buwuloorumab bati karegak di 
úyegetolaal.
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say: Di úyegetuul, jitiimalen buwuloorumab nan man jisofumi man karegak kootumi kaanoak. 
Waawu jijuke?
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind. 
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they are 
visualizing in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. Choose a good 
example you heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.

• Say: Ñaa , unaamenaal buwuloorumab bati di karegak di woololaal man jijukaal.
• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: Waawu nujuke di buwuloorumab wanaamumi di buwuloormab ban utiimalenumi di  
búyejiti?
• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at random 
asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the picture and the 
story.
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Nan uliikaalemi,nuliikaaleliik kurimak fákon , fákon. Uregaw ubajebaj kurimak juup kan 
uliikaalemi furim fákon- fákon di búkaay yanoosani.
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud
• Read aloud the story. Point to each word as you read.
Aminata di Buwuloorumab bati Fiilaf Foola.
Lakomi lakomi, di lakomi tokos!
Karim simit futok nabaje. Funak fákon nalakomi di karambaak. Bacaarab di busofoomi. Nateb 
ajiker bánaanaay, bare erorooj fatiyaay. Nalaañumi ateb ajiker kumangaak, koo poop kurorooj 
fatiyaay.
No'ona, yaŋ too galab, jiñeraañ di jípurul to fús. Keebaa najiker jo aban namumutenumi. Jiñeraaj 
di jitujulomi bánaanaay jisenumi Karim.
Karim naanujomi, "Nisalisal''
Jiñeraaj ñaa di jilaañumi jitujul fumanga jisenumi Karim. Karim nalaañumi aanujomi, "Nisalisal 
eñeraay!"
Piout, eñeraay di ejukumi wúwolumaw wati úbaaraw di katekelak, bare katekelak di fúsiilaf koom. 
Jiñeraaj jiŋoolenut jinoken di fúsiilaf.
Karim nanenumi jisinkaj joola di kupicumak koola ban naammi, "Shhh, tunten!" Karim najawumi 
di fúsiilaf man ábajulomi sileemunaas sammi di katekelak ban natey bee tíiyeŋey man asen 
sileemunaas Eñeraay.
Jiñeraaj sunsuum jo. Jiriri sileemunaas jiban di joon, "Nisalisal!" Eñeraay ebabaj uwolumaw 
wajuupoe ban di jijaw jiwubo.
Karim nalaañumi ateb ajiker bánaanaay. Nalaañumi ateb ajiker kumangaak, nalakomi ekobey yati 
apaalool mambi áleeñul man atujulool kupinaay. Bare kakamunak uke, jiñeraaj jilaañuloot inci.

3. Comprehension: During Reading (8 mins)
Factual Question: Review All
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the following factual 
questions:
      Question 1: Karim waawu namaŋe?  (bánaanaay di kumangaak)
      Question 2: Sileemunaas tótey silakoe? (Di fúsiilaf)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help pupils find the part of the 
story that contains the answer.
Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: Kareg kanookani kubabaj fúkaw.  Fúkaaf foo karegak kusankenemi mooli fo.  Di 
karegak, nijujuk eñeraay did áriiŋaaw di kuñes úwolumaw wati úbaaraw di utoj wajuupoe.  
Karegak di kulaañ kusanken mati Karim di Eñeraay di kuñes úwolumaw wati úbaaraw.  Moo 
mukaanakaan iwoonoor mati, wafaŋumi man ujuupoe di karegak mati Karim di eñeraay 
barambenoore man kubaj úwolumaw wati úbaaraw man kuri. 
• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say: Di síwoonooras faŋ so mati, ''Eñeraay di bánaanaay'' yísenoolaal yísen man Karim 
di eñeraay kurambenooremi eeno man kubaj úwolumaw wati úbaaraw man kuri; 
mati wafaŋumi man ujuupoe di karegak wan úyisenumi woo emmi Karim di Eñeraay 
kurambenoorerambenoor.  
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the story is 
mostly about.

activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet them. This 
continues all the way around the circle.
Theme Discussion
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. Put the items 
in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two pictures on the board instead.
• Say: Múmikaam moololaal di funoonaf ufe moo emmi, ''Kafatak''  Wahaw wammi di jíliibooraj 
mati múmikaam moololaal múyisenemi.
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Ure waawu?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer.
• Say: Waawu nuŋoolene uregom mati ure?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: Buu nucookooremi kafatak kooli?
• Give pupils one minute to think, even close their eyes to picture their response. Then choose 
one of the following options for discussion: call on pupils at random, Turn and Talk (have 
pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only 
if the answer is short), or have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the week.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board.  ( a, b, c )The letters should be large 
enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out in a line that is eye level for 
the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Eciikaaay uye yéyema?  Kayel kéy ebaje?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let them know if it 
is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that have been 
learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Ínje bee ewonk kayel, ookenjaat butiŋumab tan eciikaay ecila yommi, Aw di apaali di jipop 
jijaw bee di bulaakubooptey man ukoten di yan sinammi.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are having 
difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As te permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

says touch your toes. [Name] says jump twice."
• Continue with several pupils as time permits.

activities.content:

• Show the illustration of the story.
• Say: Nampi ulakaami kalaaŋenak kúceeŋak di uregaw, jíitiyejiiti ebajey kúlaaŋenak. Nan

• Call on a pupil at random to answer the question. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. 
• Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the following inferential questions:
      Question 1: Waawu kaane man eñeraay ejaw? (Ebabaj úwolumaw  wajuupoe.) 
      Question 2: Eñeraay buu erambenumi Karim? (Yoo batuje úwolumaw uceen asenwo Karim )
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct answer or

story that contains the answer.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Learn New Print Concepts
• Find a children's storybook with an author and illustrator.
• Think about how books and stories have different parts.
• Say: Nan uliikaalemi, njijukaalejuk wajuupoe wanaamutaaw di karegak. Kareg kanoosani 
kubabaj aciikaaw ooliko .
• Point to the author's name on the storybook.
• Say: Aciikaaw oo aciikumi karegak. Ay ammi aciikaaw?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by repeating, "the 
author is the person who wrote the story." 
• Say: Kareg kanoosni kabaje buwuloorum kubabaj ajoonenaaw wooliko.
• Point to the illustrator's name on the storybook.

2. Pupils trace the letters of their name on their desks or on the ground.

activities.title: Before Reading & Reason to Read
activities.content:
Comprehension: Visualization 
• Say: Moo manoomani nuliikeenaaliik karegak uke nan piyoe,tiimalenaal buwuloorumab ube di 
úyejitolaal mati karegak.
• Read the title of the story but do NOT show the illustration.
• Say: Di úyegetuul, jitiimalen buwuloorumab nan man karegak kootumi kaanoak eeno. Waawu 
jijuke?
• Give the pupils a minute to make the picture in their mind. 
• Turn and Talk: Have pupils turn to the pupil next to them to talk about what they are visualizing 
in their minds. After two minutes, gather pupils back as a group. Choose a good example you 
heard from a pupil, and share it with the class.

• Say: Ñaa unaamenaal buwuloorumab bati karegak di uwuloorumaw woololaal. 
• Show the picture for the story.
• Say: Waawu nujukumi di buwuloorumab wayesoorumi di buwuloorumab ban utiimalenumi di 
búyejetab booli.
• Give the pupils a minute to think about what was the same. Then call on a pupil at random 
asking for what they see. Make sure the pupil's description relates to the picture and the story. 
Learn New Print Concepts
• Say: Nan uliikaalemi, wulaal iliik kurimak fákon - fákon. Uregaw ubajebaj kurimak juup kan 
uliikaalemi fákon-fákon di katoj kanoosani.
• Hold up the book. Read the title slowly and point to each word.
• Call on a pupil at random to come and point to each word of the title as you read.

activities.title: Comprehension: During Reading
activities.content:
Read Aloud
• Read aloud the story. Point to each word as you read.
Ilisabet di kujaŋaak koola kugabaak 
Lakomi lakomi!  Di lakomi tokos!
Funak fákon, Iisabet di kujaŋaak koola kugabaak kulakoe tákon. Ureesaw wooliil woo emmi 
Mariyaama di Kumba, Di fukojiin fákon, Ilisabet naane kujaŋaak koola, "Kumba jaw di 
funoomenaf." Nammi Mariyaama, ''Aw pan uteb kumangaak.''  Nammi Kumba, "Aw pan uteb 
Kupomak." Ínje pan iteb sipapakaas."  Mariyama naanoomi, "Éey, ínje pan iteb so.
Bare Kumba oo naanoomi, "A'aa, ínje let iteb ko."  Ñaa Ilisabet nateb jiñiilaj di sipapakaas. 
Mariyaama natebumi kumangaak di kupomak. Bare Kumba atebut waaf.
Fúkojiin fuceen, Ilisabet nammi, "Mariyaama, jaat aw ban uteb kupomak, Kumba, aw pan uteb 
kumangaak. Ínje pan iteb sipapakaas di jiñoolom."  Mariyaama naanoomi, "Éey, ínje pan itep ko." 
Bare Kumba nammi, "A'aa, ínje let iteb ko."  Ñaa Ilisabet nateb sipapakaas di jiñoolool. Mariyaama 
nateb kupomak di kumangaak búrom.  Bare inci, Kumba atebut waaf.
Fúkojiin fákon, Mariyaama nammi, "ínje íjuut." Ilisabet naanoomi, "Ujaal bee di fusontenaf."

Karegom regom tokos!

3. Comprehension: After Reading (8 mins)
Factual Question: Review All
• Read the title of the story. Call on a pupil at random to answer each of the following factual 
Question 1: Bóbey koom di  kájeetum úwolumaw? ( funoomaf)                       
       Question 2: Waawu ubaje Mariyaama? (ajuut/batujoe)
• After each response, ask the pupil why they gave that answer. Affirm the correct answer or 
attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer. Help pupils find the part of the 
story that contains the answer.
• Inferential Questions: Main Idea
• Say: Karegak kanoosani kubabaj fujuum. Fúkaaf foo karegak kúyiisenemi di karegak.  Nijanjam  
buu kati karegak kújeetummi munoomenaam mooli bee di funoomaf .Karegak di kulammi 
kúyiisen man Lusi alatumi karambenak eeno. Moome kaanankaan iwoonoor mati , majuupoe 
di karegak yíisenyiisen buu nootaale esen fúrambenaf kulaaoorolaal.
• Ask the pupils if they agree.
• Say: Múmikaam mati karegak ''Ilisabet di kuñoolool kujaŋaak kugabaak'' muyiisen man bajumi 
fúkaw di eseney furambenaf fati kulaaoorolaal mati, majuupoe di karegak múyiisen man 
aseekaw alatumi karamben kati fiilaf foolaf.
• Repeat the sentence but prompt pupils to finish the sentence by saying what the story is 
mostly about.

activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet them. This 
continues all the way around the circle.
Theme Discussion
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. Put the items 
in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two pictures on the board instead.
• Say: Di funoomaf ufe múmikaam moololaal moo emmi  "Súukas sati eniiley" Wahaw wammi 
di fúliibaf woo emmi wati furimaf foololaal fápalo'aaf.
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle. 
• Say: Ure waawu?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer.
• Say: Waawu pan uŋoolen uregom mati ure?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item.
• Say: Waawu numaŋummi  mati fuliikitenaf? Di waawu numaŋutumi?
• Give pupils one minute to think, even close their eyes to picture their response. Then choose 
one of the following options for discussion: call on pupils at random, Turn and Talk (have 
pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and allow every pupil to answer (only 
if the answer is short), or have pupils take turns acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the week.

activities.title: Learning Sounds
activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the letters that have been learned on the board. The letters should be large enough for 
all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out in a line that is eye level for the pupils. 
After writing each letter:
• Say: Eciikaay uye yéy? Kayel kéy ebaje?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let them know if it 
is correct, and clarify the answer.

learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Pan iwonk kayelak nampi ubajumi bútiŋumab tan ekiikaay yommi, aw di apaali di jipop 
bee di bulaakubootey man jikoten ko di eciikaay.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are having 
difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.

responding when they hear the vocabulary word. They will use these words and skills during 
the read aloud.

Tujo     Funoomenaf

repeat.

the correct answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the definition.

picture of the word on the board.

activities.title: Reason to Read
activities.content:
Learn New Print Concepts
• Find a children's storybook with an author and illustrator.
• Think about how books and stories have different parts.
• Say: Nan uliikaalemi, wulaal ejuk waaf wanaamut di karegak. Kareg kanoosani kubabaj 
aciikaaw.
• Point to the author's name on the storybook.
• Say: Aciikaaw oo aciikumi karegak. Ay ammi aciikaaw?
• Give pupils a moment to think, then call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct 
answer or attempt, let them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer by repeating, "the 
author is the person who wrote the story."  
• Say: Kareg kanoosani kabajumi búrokum kañen kubabaj ajoonena.
• Point to the illustrator's name on the storybook.

the letter before continuing with the game.

and review the letter before continuing with the game.

difficulty, and consider how to give them extra support.

activities.content:
Sound Matching Game
• Write the following letters on the board:  a, b c, d e f 
• The letters should be large enough for all pupils to see. Make sure they are evenly spaced out 
in a line that is eye level for the pupils. After writing each letter:
• Say: Eciikaay uye yey? Kayel kéy ebaje?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. Affirm the correct answer or attempt, let them know if it 
is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Put the pupils into pairs and give each pair a letter card (use only the letters that have been 
learned so far). Have the pairs sit in a line facing the board.
• Say: Pan iwonk kayelak endi kayitak kan ookumi kúbabaj eciikaay, aw di apaali pan jipop bee di 
bulaakubootey man jikoten ko di eciikaay.
• When pupils go to the board with their letter card, affirm the correct answer or attempt, let 
them know if it is correct, and clarify the answer.
• Go through the letters that have been learned. Assist pupils as needed if they are having 
difficulty connecting the sound said with their letter card.
• As time permits, switch up the letter cards between the pairs of pupils.
• NOTE: Keep track of which pupils are having difficulty recognizing specific letters. Also see if 
there is a specific letter most of the class is struggling with. If this happens, stop and review 
the letter before continuing with the game.

 Ootaajaat etooŋey, pan úlantulaal uñenaw woololaal.
• .Warm up exercise: have pupils tap their fingers one at a time on their thumb (start with 
pointer, then middle, then ring, then pinky). Do one hand at a time. As pupils learn the 
movement, try doing both hands at the same time.
• Give each pupil their individual name card. 
• NOTE: Have pupils write their name on their paper. If pupils cannot complete their name, 
try to find a way to help them. For example, write the letters and have them trace. Another

kayitak.
• Have pupils come up 2-3 at a time. When they bring you their card, point to their name and 
as they say it move your finger along the letters. Then have the pupil clap the syllables in their 
name.
• NOTE: Monitor which pupils are able to identify their name and clap the syllables, and those

remember it. For example, write it in large print on their notebook or a piece of spare paper. 
Ask them to take it home and trace the letters with their finger a few times. If pupils have 
difficulty clapping the syllables in their name, clap with them as you slowly say their name.
